**Generated** from `releases/*.md` by `scripts/docs/generate-api-changelog.mjs`: 56 lines from 16 releases, out of 25 AgentDash releases read. A line is kept when it names an `/api/…` path or a method and path, a contract operation, a status code, a header, a validator, or the words route, endpoint, API, OpenAPI or contract; every line under a Deprecated, Breaking, Removed or Behaviour Change heading is kept. Lines under Tests, Testing, Validation and Contributors are not read. 2 withdrawn notes and 11 inherited upstream notes are not AgentDash releases and are skipped.

This page selects lines by their words, so it can include a line about an internal route and can miss a change worded without any of them. The release notes are the record; [the versioning policy](/api/versioning) says how a change to [the contract](/api/reference) is announced.

## v2026.1002.1 — 2026-10-02

**Changed**

- **The CoS chat never goes silent** (#981). On a hosted box every reply had started failing with Z.AI "Insufficient balance" (HTTP 429, code 1113). Z.AI bills its pay-as-you-go API and its GLM Coding Plan on separate addresses, and Hermes kept using whichever one it first reached. AgentDash now pins the Coding Plan address first, and falls back to the other only if the first does not answer. If a reply still cannot be made, the chat shows "CoS couldn't reply" with the reason and a Retry button, instead of sitting on your message forever. Replies now arrive live, without a refresh, and "CoS is thinking..." shows while you wait. Only the person who wrote a message can retry it.

**Internal**

- **Per-company sandbox spike** (#969). A prototype image and lifecycle API for running a company's agents in an isolated sandbox, with a separate signer and a per-identity network allow-list. Nothing ships or runs in a release from this yet, and it is not used by any current feature.

**Upgrade notes**

- Agents can no longer approve their own work. A work product written by an agent or an assistant grant with status `approved` or `merged` is refused with 403 `work_product_self_acceptance`. Anything that did this should hand the work to a person to Accept.

## v2026.1002.0 — 2026-10-02

**Security**

- **Bootstrap can't make you owner** (#956, #959). Setting up the CoS in an existing workspace needs its owner or admin, and never rewrites an existing role. Archived workspaces are refused. A `companyId` you aren't an active member of gets 403 with no fallback, including for instance admins. A same-email-domain signup no longer auto-joins (or owns) an existing workspace; ask its administrator for an invite.

## v2026.1001.2 — 2026-10-01

**Security**

- **Routines need permission to change** (#935, GH #710). Every routine write (create, edit, run, trigger create, update, delete and secret rotation) needs `tasks:assign`; agents always get 403. A company import containing recurring tasks runs the same check before writing anything, and imported routines arrive paused.

## v2026.1001.1 — 2026-10-01

**Changed**

- **An exhausted recovery budget holds until a named person acts:** A board user clears the block with **Clear recovery block & retry** (`POST /issues/:id/recovery-budget/clear`), which also resumes automatic retries. Clearing while a one-run authorization is pending cancels that run and records it.
- **An exhausted recovery budget holds until a named person acts:** Or a person authorizes **exactly one run** while the block stays: **Authorize one run** on the issue page (a review then confirm dialog), or `task_recovery.remediate` through `/api/human-control` with a named board key. That run can't continue on its own; the authorization expires after 15 minutes by default.
- **An exhausted recovery budget holds until a named person acts:** Who can authorize: company admins, holders of `agents:create`, and the agent's steward, accountable person or creator. Plain members and viewers see the block but get `403`, also through board keys.

**Fixed**

- **The Agent visibility setting now reads back.** Company reads went through an explicit column list that did not include `agentVisibilityDefault`, so `GET /companies/:id` and the `PATCH` response never carried it. The server enforced the saved value (the rule reads the column directly), but the radio under Settings › Members & access always showed *Everyone sees every agent*, whatever an administrator had saved. The column is in the list, and the route test now asserts the value on both the read and the write response.
- A `400 Invalid identifier` is logged at warn with the route and parameter names (#900).
- The model-key nudge cooldown is atomic, and `/billing/status` answers `404` for an unknown company (#843).

## v2026.1001.0 — 2026-10-01

**Added**

- **Agent visibility:** What a member cannot see is absent from every list and `404` on its id — agents, issues, approvals, activity, the dashboard, sidebar badges, org chart, heartbeat and live runs, and live-event delivery — the same rule restricted projects already enforce.
- **Named-human control plane** (#883; migration `0141_human_action_handles`). `/api/human-control` (`identity`, `discover`, `read`, `prepare`, `confirm`) for a verified named board key only. Handles are hashed, bound to user, key, target, operation and payload, expire after 15 minutes, and are claimed atomically before execution. `AGENTDASH_TOOLSET=human` exposes the matching MCP tools. Expired handles are swept hourly. Documented in `doc/HUMAN-CONTROL.md`.

**Changed**

- **One shell for every company:** `GET /companies/:id/me/agent` and the assign route now answer `404` in a company without stewardship, before any agent or stewardship row is created. Creating an agent pairs its creator as steward only where stewardship is on.
- **Recovery budget clears only on Clear** (#877). Moving an issue out of `blocked`, commenting to reopen it, or reassigning it no longer clears an exhausted recovery budget; `POST /issues/:id/recovery-budget/clear` is the only clear. A run a person starts directly still goes ahead; automatic, linked, agent-, system- and assistant-started wakes are refused while the marker stands. PATCH and comment responses carry a `recoveryBudgetNotice` while it does.
- **Issue acceptance re-checks current authority** (#881). PATCH, comment and tree writes re-read the caller's credential, membership, grants, project access and every selected row under share locks, then re-check immediately before the write; field changes, comment, execution decision, references and audits commit in one transaction, and live events publish only after commit. An explicit but invalid `Bearer` or `x-agent-key` header is unauthenticated rather than falling back to the local operator. The restricted-project guard now covers agents too. Seven acceptance blocks are added to the default agent mandate.

## v2026.930.1 — 2026-09-30

**Fixed**

- **Live updates respect project access:** Each socket now gets only the events for projects it can see, using the same rule as the REST routes. An event that can't be resolved to a project is dropped for anyone who doesn't see everything, but only in companies with a restricted project.
- **Related issues, ancestors, blocker ids and feedback traces respect project access:** `blockedByIssueIds` on create, child create and PATCH is checked like other body ids. A restricted, unknown or other-company blocker id now returns `404 Blocker issue not found` (was `422` for an unknown id). A PATCH by someone off the list keeps restricted blockers they can't see.
- **Related issues, ancestors, blocker ids and feedback traces respect project access:** Feedback trace lists hide restricted traces, and single-trace reads return 404.
- **Related issues, ancestors, blocker ids and feedback traces respect project access:** `GET /assistant/pending-decisions` blanks a restricted linked issue.
- **OTA updater:** `/api/health` now reports `releaseCommit` when the server runs from a release directory. After a restart, the updater waits until health reports the target commit, and rolls back if it doesn't.

**Also in v2026.930.0, missing from its notes**

- **Invalid ids return 400 on every route** (#855). Any uuid-cast error (Postgres 22P02) now returns `400 Invalid identifier` and is no longer logged as a server error, not only on the bridge routes.

**Upgrade notes**

- An API client that relied on `422` for an unknown blocker id now gets `404`.

## v2026.930.0 — 2026-09-30

**Fixed**

- **Terminating an agent ends its stewardship:** Only that agent's channel bindings are revoked. The person's bridge endpoints are untouched.
- **A stale hire approval can no longer terminate a working agent:** Rejecting a hire whose agent is already active returns 409, and the Override page warns and disables reject in that case.
- **Restricted projects:** on every `/issues/:id/*` route;
- **Run logs** (#851). A run that never started returns an empty log (`200`, `missing: true`) instead of a 404.
- **Bridge ids** (#855). A malformed `endpointId` or `taskId` returns 400 instead of a database 500.

**Upgrade notes**

- **Stricter validation.** Bridge `taskClass` values other than `read` or `act` now get 400 instead of silently becoming `read`.

**Known issues**

- Project access is not yet applied to plugin routes, feedback traces, relation summaries, the verdict list or tree descendants.

## v2026.927.0 — 2026-09-27

**Added**

- **Assistant MCP work tools** (#745): `start_project`, `create_work_item`, `assign_work`, `comment_on_work` and `update_work_item`, available to grants with the `work` scope. Retries are safe: a repeated call returns the original item instead of creating a duplicate. Writes are limited to five exact routes and an allowlist of body fields, capped at 30 writes and 10 new issues per grant per hour, and every write is logged with the grant id.
- **Release image** (#774): each stable release publishes `ghcr.io/thetangstr/agentdash:v2026.927.0` for amd64 and arm64, and records its digest in the GitHub Release. `/api/health` reports `releaseTag` (#752).

**Upgrade notes**

- **Secret names beginning `github-token-` are reserved.** Creating or renaming a secret to one returns 422. An existing secret with such a name is hidden from the list and ignored in agent, project and environment configuration, and an SSH environment that references one returns 422.

## v2026.925.0 — 2026-09-25

**Added**

- **OAuth 2.1 for assistants** (#688). The instance is its own authorization server: `/.well-known/oauth-*`, `/oauth/register|authorize|token|revoke` and a remote streamable-HTTP endpoint at `/api/mcp/assistant`. PKCE S256 only, single-use codes, rotating refresh tokens, DCR and CIMD, and a built-in `muse` client pinned to Meta's callback. An assistant token (`pcpa_`) reaches no raw REST route. Tools read through a short-lived in-process credential instead.

**Upgrade notes**

- **New public endpoints on every install:** the OAuth metadata and endpoints above, plus `/api/mcp/assistant`. Anyone can register a client without signing in (30 clients by default).
- **Project env:** execution-affecting keys (for example `PATH`, `GIT_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `OPENAI_*`, `HERMES_*`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`) are dropped at run time, including keys saved before this release. Any edit that still includes one, or a key that isn't upper-case, returns 422. Remove those keys before editing a project's env.
- **Agent keys:** an agent can change only `name`, `title`, `icon` and `capabilities` on itself, plus `desiredSkills` on another agent. A CEO-agent routine that edits role, status, reporting line, budget, runtime or adapter config now gets a 403.

## v2026.923.0 — 2026-09-23

**Added**

- **No address is ever hard-coded.** Guides carry the token `{{instanceUrl}}`; the page substitutes what this instance publishes (`publicBaseUrl` from `/api/health`), falling back to the browser origin — the same rule the connect command follows. The same files are listed in `docs/docs.json`, so the docs site and the app share one source.

**Changed**

- `UnprefixedBoardRedirect` and `NoCompaniesStartPage` moved unchanged from `App.tsx` into `components/UnprefixedBoardRedirect.tsx`, so a route test can mount the real redirect beside the real pages.
- `guides` is registered as a board route root in `lib/company-routes.ts`, so the prefix helpers never read `/guides/...` as a company code. CI caught the omission; the existing `company-routes` test is what caught it.

## v2026.922.0 — 2026-09-22

**Behaviour Change**

- **Never the evidence.** The approval payload does not appear in any delivered message.
- **Never a decision handle.** The digest is built handle-less for webhooks — the first implementation minted callback tokens and the foreign key refused it; zero such rows is now the specification.
- **The steward's own.** Registration, listing and revocation exist only under `me/`; the URL never returns whole (host hint only); every registration and revocation is audited.

## v2026.908.0 — 2026-09-08

**Also In This Release**

- Four empty states stopped reporting a failed load as an empty one. A query error read as zero results, so a page whose request had 500'd said there was nothing waiting.

## v2026.904.0 — 2026-09-05

**The Steward Inbox**

- **A steward can direct work and set a preference from the same surface.** Naming an agent and a task ("have Casper draft the agenda") resolves the agent, reads the assignment back, and acts only when the person confirms a single-use handle bound to that machine — nothing happens on the strength of a sentence alone, and a name that does not resolve comes back as a question, never a guess. The same propose-then-confirm shape governs the one preference offered (check every 30 or 60 minutes). Across this release the endpoint credential's allowlist grows from three routes (poll, result, decline) to nine — the six inbox routes for sync, ack, decide, agents, propose, and confirm — with no new authority: permission is re-checked when the handle is redeemed, a handle is inert on any other machine including the same person's second one, and the work is attributed to the person, never the machine.

**Honest Surfaces**

- **A wrong method on a known route answers 405** with an `Allow` header computed from the router itself. Unknown paths still answer 404.
- **Every agent API key records what minted it** — agent creation, onboarding, a connect code, or a person at the keys panel — with the creating user or agent where there was one. The keys panel says so in words, and the agent-creation response marks its bundled key `autoCreated: true`.

**Known Limitations, Stated Plainly**

- The person accountable for an autonomous agent still cannot read the governance policy enforced on that agent — the read answers 403 because autonomous agents hold no stewardship row. The one-route fix (#598) is approved and lands after 1.0; the candidate was frozen without it.

## v2026.902.0 — 2026-09-02

**Truthful Signals**

- **Run health is measured, not claimed.** Every health indicator on an agent was a claim made before the fact. The run records knew better: one agent had failed 163 of 304 runs and left no evidence on 114 of the 137 that succeeded. Agent detail now carries `runHealth`, and the companies list carries a `runsSucceededWithoutEvidence` ratio. Expect that ratio to look bad on existing fleets — it is the true number surfaced for the first time, not a regression.
- **`PATCH /agents/:id` no longer lies about stewards.** It answered `200` to a `steward` field and changed nothing, because zod stripped the undeclared key before the handler saw it. It now returns `422` and names the real endpoint.
- **Agents can resolve a person.** `GET /companies/:id/people` returns identity only — no assignment authority — so an agent asked to act on someone by name no longer has to guess an email and then report a colleague as not being a member.

**Over-the-Air Updates: Foundations and Apply Path**

- Read-only `GET /api/instance/ota/status` exposes installed version, available release with verbatim notes, a diff summary, database compatibility, and a rollback plan.
- Approval is a request/decide ceremony bound to the commit and stamped with the compatibility verdict at consent time. **There is no apply route** — the server records consent; a separate privileged process acts.

## v2026.827.1 — 2026-08-27

**Critical OTA Correction**

- **Native macOS readiness now parses correctly** — The source-checkout release-control asset now escapes the `Bearer ` case pattern in the generated readiness wrapper so the macOS system Bash can parse and run the canonical post-restart health gate.

## v2026.827.0 — 2026-08-27

**Highlights**

- **Agent output persists through the supported run-attributed surface** — Worker guidance now includes the correct issue-comment endpoint, bearer identity, and run attribution header, while paired steward harnesses can reach their narrowly scoped directive and governance controls. (#531)

**Improvements**

- **Bounded idle polling** — Due checks respect the configured heartbeat interval, coalesce against active runs, and retain the existing wakeworthy-work contract without recurring idle model calls. (#530)
